1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night

Rain had been falling on the village of Doldari for three days straight. Kim Haneul's older sister had left for Seoul in the spring, and ever since, Haneul had been running the village's little apothecary shop on her own.
When dusk settled, she closed the shutters, counted the day's earnings, put out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had just lain down when an urgent pounding sounded on the door below, followed by a man's voice. "Is anyone there?"

A young man stood at the door, soaked to the skin. The cloth wrapped around his left arm was stained through with blood. He introduced himself as Park Junho and said he was with the Azure Dragon Society.
"Please, tend to my wound," Park Junho said in a low voice. "I'll pay you. Would three thousand five hundred nyang be enough?"
He drew a letter wrapped in oilpaper from inside his coat. "This letter has to reach Cheongpungsa by the eighteenth of May."
Haneul thought it over. The neighbors were already sore with envy over how well the apothecary was doing, and now a strange man had come knocking in the middle of the night.
Even so, Haneul refused the money and said only, "I'll guide you up the mountain first thing tomorrow morning."
2: As soon as day broke, the two of them set out. Haneul carried a basket on her back, and inside it were rice balls, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they came across an old man, Lee Youngsoo, chopping firewood. The old man set down his axe and lowered his voice. The evening before, three strangers had been at the edge of the village, asking after a wounded young man.
"Haneul, take the side path," Lee Youngsoo said. "The main road is dangerous." Haneul thanked the old man.
The side path was narrow and slippery. Haneul led the way, planting each step firmly as she went. Park Junho followed behind in silence.

By noon the rain had stopped and the mountain mist slowly lifted, and the roof of Cheongpungsa came into view in the distance. In front of the temple gate stood a Buddhist nun. It was the nun Jeonghye, whose duty at the temple was to receive visitors.
The nun Jeonghye took the letter, checked the red seal on it, and nodded. "The abbot has been waiting two years for this letter."
Park Junho said to Haneul, "I owe you my life." Haneul smiled and answered, "Then next time you come, you can fix the roof of the medicine shop." Park Junho stayed at the temple.
Toward evening, Haneul came down the mountain alone. By the time she arrived home, it was already dark. She lit the lamp and sat for a long while behind the counter.
